title: Literary Arts and Narrative Design
answer: Agentic drafting, outlining, character dialogue, continuity tracking and developmental editing.

children.name: Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows
children.blurb: Agentic drafting and multi-model workflows describe a way of writing in which a language model is given a goal and a degree of autonomy, then allowed to plan, draft, revise and check its own output across several passes, often handing parts of the job to other models.

children.name: Outlining and Plot Structure
children.blurb: Outlining and plot structure covers the planning layer of narrative work, the stage where a story's events are ordered, its turns placed, and its ending decided before or alongside drafting.

children.name: Character Voice and Dialogue
children.blurb: Character voice and dialogue covers the craft of making a fictional person sound like themselves on the page, in a script, or in a game, and it now includes the use of language models to draft, extend, or test that speech.

children.name: World-Building and Continuity
children.blurb: World-building and continuity is the craft of keeping a fictional setting coherent across many pieces of work, whether that is a novel series, a game franchise, a television writers room or a tabletop campaign.

children.name: Developmental Editing
children.blurb: Developmental editing is the work of shaping a manuscript at the level of structure, argument, character and pacing rather than at the level of commas and typos.

sections.body: Literary arts and narrative design covers the use of artificial intelligence in the making of fiction and long form prose, from the first sketch of a premise to the final revision pass. In practice, writers now use language models to generate draft scenes, propose alternative phrasings, expand sparse outlines into full chapters, and produce variant dialogue for a single exchange. Agentic setups go further, letting a model plan a sequence of drafting steps, call different models for different jobs, and assemble a manuscript section by section. Continuity work is one of the clearest current uses, where a system scans a long manuscript for contradictions in names, dates, physical details and established facts. Developmental editing tools summarize chapters, flag pacing problems, and suggest structural changes at the level of acts and arcs.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is genuinely useful at the level of generation and checking, and much less reliable at the level of judgment. Producing fluent prose is largely solved, and so is mechanical continuity checking across a long document when the system is given the full text. What is not solved is sustained coherence over hundreds of pages, since models drift, forget earlier decisions, and quietly invent details that conflict with what came before. Voice is a persistent weak point, because generated dialogue tends toward a generic register unless heavily constrained by examples and rules. Structural advice from these systems is often plausible sounding but shallow, and it cannot weigh a book against the intentions of its author. The honest limit is that these tools assist a writer's decisions rather than make them, and any output needs human reading before it counts as a draft.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the arc of a manuscript. Outlining and Plot Structure is the entry point, covering how a premise becomes a beat sheet or chapter plan and where models help or flatten that work. Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows then takes that plan into production, describing pipelines where one model plans, another drafts, and a third revises, along with the coordination problems that arise. Character Voice and Dialogue narrows to the line level, on keeping speech distinct and consistent across a cast. World-Building and Continuity handles the reference layer, the tracking of places, timelines and established facts so a long project does not contradict itself. Developmental Editing sits at the end, on revision at the scale of the whole book, where structure, pacing and theme are assessed and changes proposed. A reader can move through them in that order or go straight to the one matching the stage of their own project.
